Title: Dynamic Modeling of Microalgae Growth and Lipid Production under Transient Light and Nitrogen Conditions

Abstract: ABSTRACT: We developed a new dynamic model to characterize how light and nitrogen regulate the cellular processes of photosynthetic microalgae leading to transient changes in the production of neutral lipids, carbohydrates, and biomass. Our model recapitulated the versatile neutral lipid synthesis pathways via (i) carbon reuse from carbohydrate metabolism under nitrogen sufficiency and (ii) fixed carbon redirection under nitrogen depletion. We also characterized the effects of light adaptation, light inhibition hysteresis, and nitrogen limitation on photosynthetic carbon fixation. Model: Dynamic microalgae growth and lipid production model
Laws:
(9) [constitutive] Absorbance per unit length is computed by weighting the Chl-a and non-Chl-a carbon concentrations by their optical cross sections.
(10) [constitutive] The reactor-average light intensity is obtained by averaging the attenuated local light intensity over the optical path.
(11) [constitutive] The reference average light intensity is calculated by averaging the unattenuated local light intensity over the optical path.
(12) [constitutive] Photosynthesis per functional biomass follows a light-response curve with light limitation, saturation, and inhibition at high intensity.
(13) [constitutive] The light-saturation intensity is adjusted according to maximum fixation capacity, total cellular carbon, light-energy yield, and Chl-a content.
(14) [constitutive] The effective carbon yield on light energy decreases exponentially with reference average irradiance.
(15) [constitutive] The fraction of carbon redirected from carbohydrate to lipid accumulation rises as nitrate concentration falls, approaching its maximum fraction under nitrate limitation.
(16) [constitutive] Chl-a degradation is scaled by nitrate-starvation and high-light stress responses, increasing at low nitrate and higher reference irradiance.
(17) [constitutive] Nitrate uptake per functional biomass increases with extracellular nitrate normalized to its initial concentration and is downregulated as the cellular nitrogen quota approaches its maximum.
(18) [definition] The cellular nitrogen quota is computed as cellular nitrogen concentration divided by total cellular carbon concentration.

States (computed by the ODEs):
- X_{cd}: Concentration of functional biomass (algal biomass excluding carbohydrates and neutral lipids) as C
- X_{carb}: Concentration of carbohydrates as C
- X_{nl}: Concentration of neutral lipids as C
- X_{chl}: Concentration of Chl-a as C
- S_{NO3}: Concentration of nitrate as N in the reactor
- X_{N}: Concentration of cellular nitrogen as N

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- X_{C}: Total cellular carbon concentration, used to represent non-Chl-a biomass together with X_{chl}.
- S_{NO3_0}: Initial nitrate concentration

Model-wide assumptions:
- Optical cross‑section parameters a and b are taken as constant regardless of cultivation conditions.
- The composition of functional biomass is fixed to CH1.8O0.5N0.2.
- Nitrate uptake is assumed to equal the nitrate removed from the medium.

answer.description: This dynamic model describes Dunaliella viridis cultivation in a flat-panel photobioreactor under changing light and nitrogen conditions, predicting functional biomass, carbohydrates, neutral lipids, chlorophyll-a, nitrate, and cellular nitrogen. It combines light attenuation and photosynthetic light responses with quota-regulated nitrate uptake, nitrogen-dependent carbon allocation, and stress-related chlorophyll-a degradation; the operating mode is not stated in the supplied text.
